headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: ECC can write/modify shared state while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and undocumented for interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared communication surface or runnable output channel; B can read/write files, use MCP, and parse stdin/stdout, so only a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry instructions. That makes prompt injection plausible but not default. The pair lacks documented direct ingestion from A into B.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's stdin/stdout or files
IF A is wrapped in a shared filesystem or MCP bridge not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted A outputs into B
Use a provenance note before feeding A outputs to B
Restrict B MCP servers to trusted sources only

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network_egress none, while B touches session files, git history, docs, and security findings and can write files and call APIs. The pair does not show a shared workspace, so leakage is possible mainly through operator-mediated file transfer or shared local state, not by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF A outputs are saved into files that B reads or uploads
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid placing secrets in shared project files
Review B's API destinations before enabling it
Clear session files after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted local write, git mutation, shell, and browser capabilities; A is non-runnable and shows no write surface, so direct conflict is limited. However, B's default multi-instance state and shared-state warning mean collisions are plausible if both are attached to the same repo or home directory. Uncertainty about A's runtime surface keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or home directory
IF B runs multiple instances without separate roots
mitigations: Assign separate roots per instance
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Turn on file locking for shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on files, git, browsers, and APIs, so if it consumes A's course content or generated text as authoritative input, errors can propagate into downstream work. A is non-runnable and not documented as producing verified facts, so the main risk is operator-mediated chaining rather than an autonomous loop. That still fits medium because B has action-taking authority.
conditions: IF A outputs are treated as facts or instructions by B
IF B commits, posts, or executes actions based on unverified A content
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Use a verification checklist before commits or API calls
Limit B to read-only mode during evaluation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data class is documented for A, so a residency or certification mismatch is not evidenced. B does handle session data, git history, and security findings, but the profiles do not show a regulated-data transfer path from A to B. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into A or B outside the profiles
IF B's API destinations are used for regulated content
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent
Confirm retention settings for B session files
Review OAuth scopes before enabling GitHub App access
Keep audit logs of data transfers
